question: What are strong baselines model is compared to?

answer.free_form_answer:
Baseline models are:
- Chen et al., 2015a
- Chen et al., 2015b
- Liu et al., 2016
- Cai and Zhao, 2016
- Cai et al., 2017
- Zhou et al., 2017
- Ma et al., 2018
- Wang et al., 2019
evidence: Tables TABREF25 and TABREF26 reports the performance of recent models and ours in terms of closed test setting. Without the assistance of unsupervised segmentation features userd in BIBREF20, our model outperforms all the other models in MSR and AS except BIBREF18 and get comparable performance in PKU and CITYU. Note that all the other models for this comparison adopt various $n$-gram features while only our model takes unigram ones.

title: Attention Is All You Need for Chinese Word Segmentation
answer_short: strong baselines in terms of closed test setting
answer_rationale: The strong baselines are compared to in terms of performance and speed, particularly in the context of Chinese word segmentation models using attention mechanisms. The evidence from Text 1 explicitly states that the proposed attention-only model achieves new state-of-the-art or comparable performance against strong baselines in terms of closed test setting.
